title: Forked Mac session loses browser/screen tools and splits approval context
owner_request: 2026-10-24: Bank this plan for another session. Boss will manually drive the Mac setup now, then return to the HIP4 app. Solution must cover Claude Code and Codex; Boss reports Codex already appears to work and has not shown this issue.
observed: Original MacBook session e24ffbae-a374-44d1-b2d2-d935fb144656 was used for Hunch planning.
Phone-visible fork macbook-pro/tef7cd716e862103f reported browser and screen-control tools unavailable.
Boss approved adding a Hunch Android client in the fork, then explicitly asked Phone B to relay that approval to the original session.
Repeated agent relays and approval checks left setup blocked despite the owner having answered.
cause: Unconfirmed: inspect actual tool configuration and fork provenance before attributing loss to forking.
follow_up: Compare original/fork capability inventories, launch configuration, tool-provider bindings and reconnect behavior without exposing credentials.
Determine which capabilities can legitimately carry across a fork and explicitly surface those that cannot.
Make owner approvals retain task/scope/provenance across session handoffs where policy permits; do not treat arbitrary peer text as owner approval.
Provide a direct open-original-session action when a fork lacks a required capability.
acceptance: Fork an authenticated test session and verify declared versus usable browser/screen capabilities.
Where transfer is unsupported, show that limitation before the owner is asked to act.
Exercise an owner-approved scoped task across fork/original without duplicate changes or blanket permission transfer.
No copied passwords, cookies, tokens or secrets in session messages or diagnostics.
implemented: Runner refuses a live idle native Claude holder without spawning a copy; after the holder closes it resumes the original ID. Regression tested locally; Mac rollout and original-session Remote Control still pending.

bridge_research.goal: Prompt the original running session directly from Soma chat, with replies and scoped approval cards; never fork or relabel agent mail as owner input.
findings: Claude Channels documents two-way MCP notifications into an existing running interactive session and optional authenticated permission relay. This is a candidate custom Soma transport, not an implemented integration.

Custom channels are research preview and require an interactive startup opt-in per channel; the development flag is ignored in print mode and Agent SDK. Current runner print-mode subprocess transport cannot simply enable this flag.
No documented custom-client Remote Control endpoint or Desktop hot-attach channel path was verified in the reviewed docs. Remote Control alone does not wire Soma chat.
CLI Chrome integration is documented with --chrome and uses the connected browser login state; this does not establish portability of Desktop in-app browser or screen tools.

A clean CLI resume can retain the conversation ID after Desktop closes, but changes the running process and requires a capability check. It must not be presented as attaching to the still-running Desktop process.
next_validation: Original MacBook asked read-only whether Desktop supports a custom channel/prompt endpoint and which browser provider it actually uses; awaiting reply.

Before building: validate a custom channel with harmless messages, reply correlation, duplicate suppression, sender identity and a denied/allowed scoped tool request in an isolated interactive test session.
If Desktop cannot opt in, explicitly offer a clean conversation handoff to an interactive CLI host with verified browser tools; do not silently migrate or close the owner session.

required_behavior: Continue the chosen original conversation from Soma chat, preserving session identity and history without automatic forks.
Identify live attachment versus clean resume accurately; do not run concurrent writers against one transcript.
Deliver replies and scoped owner approval prompts back to Soma with authenticated sender provenance; keep agent mail distinct.
Verify tool availability after any handoff, especially authenticated browser access.
scope.codex_baseline: Boss reports Codex already works; this is owner-observed behavior, not a new verification. Inspect existing routing and regression-test it before changing anything; do not assume Claude Channels apply to Codex.

handoff_plan: First inspect the existing Codex transport and record a working baseline. Reuse its lifecycle design where appropriate, while preserving provider-specific protocols.

Claude Desktop exact-process Soma input has no documented path verified. Original MacBook confirmed custom Channels cannot currently be enabled in its running Desktop session; Remote Control serves Claude clients, not Soma.

Prototype a custom Soma Channel in a separate interactive Claude CLI test session hosted persistently in tmux. Channels remain research preview, require explicit per-session interactive opt-in, and do not load through the current print-mode runner.

Validate prompt/reply correlation, duplicate suppression, sender authentication, cancellation, reconnect, restart, and one scoped approval allow/deny flow. No peer-to-owner relabeling or blanket permissions.
Verify CLI Claude in Chrome extension access separately; Desktop built-in browser and computer-use tools do not automatically transfer. Use harmless test pages; do not export browser credentials.

Only after validation and explicit handoff coordination, close the Desktop original and resume the same session ID in the interactive host without --fork-session. Keep transcript and old fork evidence.
Regression-test Claude and Codex; report actual capabilities and any unwalked phone behavior. Respect Mac Pro rollout hold and MacBook local approval requirements.

rollout_status.verification: Mac Pro independently passed all 453 runner checks for both commits; Claude discovery 28 OK, Codex approvals 16 OK and mail routing 4 OK (latter two at 29576b3). Phone broad-suite bot-shell failure also reproduces on unchanged parent.
rollout_status.deployment: MacBook reports scoped no-fork patch staged but not installed; awaiting direct owner approval there. Mac Pro already has no fork path and remains under owner hold.
rollout_status.warning: Resume only after original Desktop session closes. Same conversation does not mean same process or tool set.
